commitResults.messageTitle: Add a few representative use cases

commitResults.messageBody:
The feature spec requires the functionality of importing contacts in
bulk from an external file so the model needs a type for this class.
The path can be relative to the root project directory or absolute.
The CSV file must minimally contain a name and class column since a
person is uniquely identified by those two attributes. Column headers
are mandatory but case-insensitive and order-independent.

commitResults.messageBody: Add use cases to DG

The feature spec requires prefixes such as /name and /class instead of
the short n/ and p/ forms.

Make the tokenizer recognize a prefix only when it is preceded by
whitespace and followed by whitespace or the end of the input, so that
/class does not match inside /classroom.

List the prefixes in duplicate-prefix errors in the order they were
checked.

Update the test helpers and the add-related UG and DG examples.

Add ArgumentTokenizer#findUnrecognizedPrefixes, which returns the
whitespace-delimited tokens that start with a slash but are not one of
the given prefixes. Parsers can use it to reject such input.

Names accepted digits and any mix of letters and spaces, and were
compared case-sensitively.

Restrict names to the letters A-Z and a-z, spaces and the characters
' - . /, starting with a letter and at most 80 characters. A slash is
only valid between two letters, as in s/o.

Compare names ignoring case and extra whitespace, while keeping the
text as typed for display. Report a separate error for empty, too long
and invalid-character names, in the parser and when loading storage.

The feature spec identifies a contact by name and class, so the model
needs a type for the class.

Add ClassName, which accepts letters, digits, spaces and the characters
- . _, starts with a letter or digit and has at most 80 characters.
Class names are compared ignoring case and extra whitespace, while the
text is kept as typed for display.

Move the comparison key logic from Name into StringUtil so that both
classes share it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add class and optional email to Person
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts are now identified by name and class, and email is optional.

Add a ClassName field to Person and make Email optional, exposed as an
Optional from Person#getEmail. Two persons are the same when their
names and classes match, ignoring case and extra whitespace.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove phone and address from Person
commitResults.messageBody:
Neither field is part of the new contact model.

Delete Phone and Address, along with their parsing, storage and display
code and the /phone and /address prefixes. The add command no longer
accepts them. Old phone and address keys in existing data files are
ignored when loading.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update add command messages and validation
Add name and class lookup to Person
commitResults.messageBody:
The delete command will look up a contact by the name and class that
the user types. These may not be valid, so they cannot be turned into
Name or ClassName objects.

Add Name#matches and ClassName#matches, which compare a raw string with
the stored value, ignoring case and extra whitespace, and
Person#hasNameAndClass, which uses them. Text that is not a valid name
or class does not match and does not cause an error.

commitResults.messageTitle: Split DeleteCommand into index and name forms
commitResults.messageBody:
Delete by name and class is being added next to the existing delete by
index. Both need the same success message and the same deletion step.

Make DeleteCommand an abstract base holding the shared usage and
success messages and a helper that deletes a person and reports who was
deleted. Move the existing behavior into DeleteByIndexCommand, which
still acts on the displayed list.

The success message now shows the deleted person's name and class
instead of all their details.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add delete by name and class
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts can now be deleted by name and class as well as by index,
because the same name may appear in several classes.

Add DeleteByNameAndClassCommand, which searches the whole address book
regardless of any filter, ignoring case and extra whitespace. The
parser accepts either an index or the /name and /class parameters, and
reports problems in the same order as the add command, with "No contact
found" when nothing matches.

Share the missing name and class messages and the unrecognized
parameter check between the add and delete parsers.

commitResults.messageTitle: Adapt edit command to the new Person model
commitResults.messageBody:
Person no longer has a phone or address and now has a class and an
optional email, so the edit command, its parser and their tests no
longer compile.

Remove the phone and address options and keep the class when editing,
as a minimal fix so that the project builds and its tests pass. This is
a temporary fix. The edit command is to be reworked properly
in the future.

commitResults.messageTitle: List command: Accept at most one argument
commitResults.messageBody:
The list command ignored all arguments, so "list John Doe" silently
listed everyone. The specification now requires extra arguments to be
rejected, and a later search feature will give a single argument
meaning.

Add ListCommandParser, which accepts no argument or exactly one
argument and rejects more with the standard invalid command format
message. The single argument is currently ignored and the success
message is unchanged.

The list command rejected more than one argument, which would prevent
searching for a multi-word name or class such as "John Doe" once list
supports a keyword.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add PersonMatchesKeyword predicate for list search
commitResults.messageBody:
Searching contacts by keyword needs one check that looks at a person's
name, class and tags together. The existing name predicate only
matches whole words in names.

Add PersonMatchesKeyword, which accepts a person if the keyword is a
contiguous substring of the name, class name or any tag name. Case and
extra whitespace are ignored, so multi-word names and classes can be
searched.

commitResults.messageTitle: List command: Filter persons by keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
The list command always showed every person, even though the keyword
search matches persons by name, class or tag.

Let ListCommand take an optional PersonMatchesKeyword predicate. Without
one it still lists everyone with the existing message. With one it
shows only the matching persons and reports how many were listed,
including zero when nobody matches. The usage message now describes the
keyword.

commitResults.messageTitle: List command: Parse argument as search keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
The list command parser accepted any argument but ignored it, so
"list John" still listed everyone.

Pass the trimmed argument to ListCommand as a PersonMatchesKeyword.
The whole argument is one keyword, so a full name or class such as
"John Doe" can be searched. Empty arguments still list all persons.

Tag command: Link contacts to a group
commitResults.messageBody:
- Add TagCommand, which links the contacts at the given indices of the
  displayed list to a group
- Make it atomic: it checks every index and every membership before
  changing any contact, so a failure never leaves some contacts linked
- Report all indices that are not in the displayed list, and all
  contacts already in the group, in a single error each
- List the linked contacts as "Name (Class)" in the success message so
  that contacts sharing a name can be told apart
- Document the command and the failure cases (UC04) in the Developer
  Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag command: Parse group and members
commitResults.messageBody:
- Add TagCommandParser for the format
  "tag /group GROUP_NAME /members INDEX[,INDEX]..."
- Report problems in a fixed order: unknown parameters, repeated
  parameters, text before the first parameter, missing group, missing
  members, invalid group name, then invalid members. This follows
  AddCommandParser, so both commands behave alike
- Treat a parameter given without a value as missing, so that
  "/members" alone says the members are missing instead of reporting
  an empty entry
- Reject the form without prefixes, such as "tag GroupA 1 3", as an
  invalid command format
- Register the "tag" command word in AddressBookParser so that the user
  can run the command

Tags were sorted by their exact text, so uppercase names came before
lowercase ones ("Zeta" before "alpha"). Tag casing is now whatever the
user typed, so this looked random.

- Sort the tags shown on a contact card alphabetically, ignoring case
- Move the sorting into getSortedTags so it can be unit tested without
  starting JavaFX

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for the sample data
commitResults.messageBody:
Coverage dropped slightly after the add command was merged, mostly
because the sample data is not exercised by any test.

Check that the sample persons are valid, have distinct identities, span
several classes and include a person without an email, and that the
sample address book contains them. Also test getTagSet.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag command: Improve Javadoc and code style
commitResults.messageBody:
Some private helpers in ParserUtil, Tag and TagCommand had no Javadoc,
the argument that keeps trailing empty entries in String#split was an
unexplained -1, and a few lines went over the 110 character soft limit.
The TagCommand constructor also said that duplicate indices are not
allowed without checking it. A repeated index would make the command
change the same contact twice and fail halfway, which breaks the
all-or-nothing behavior.

This adds the missing Javadoc, names the split argument, and wraps the
long lines. The constructor now asserts that no index is repeated, which
the parser already guarantees, and a test covers the assertion.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parsers: Share the unrecognized prefix check
Tag tests: Rename and split multi-scenario tests
commitResults.messageBody:
TagTest, PersonTest and TagCommandTest each had tests such as equals,
hasTag and withTag that checked many scenarios in one method, so a
failure did not say which scenario broke and the names did not follow
the featureUnderTest_testScenario_expectedBehavior convention. The
TagCommandTest equals test was also over the 30 line guideline.

Each of these scenarios is now its own test with a name that states the
scenario and the expected result. The assertions are the same, except
that the withTag test for a contact without an email now also checks
that the copy still has no email. The tests that came with the original
code, such as PersonTest.equals, are left as they were.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag tests: Cover storage and LogicManager
commitResults.messageBody:
The tag command was only tested through its parser and command classes.
Nothing checked that a group name with spaces or mixed casing survives
being saved and loaded, that an over-long tag in the data file is
rejected, or that running tag through LogicManager saves the address
book on success and leaves it unsaved on failure.

JsonAdaptedPersonTest now covers the round trip of tags as typed, the
normalizing of extra spaces in a data file, and an over-long tag.
LogicManagerTest runs tag with a valid command and checks the saved
file, and with the already-in-group, missing-index and missing-members
failures, checking that nothing is saved for the first two.

commitResults.messageTitle: User Guide: Include the tag command

commitResults.messageBody:
The DG described the tag command but left out a few things that a new
developer would need. It did not say how tags are stored in the data
file or why the TagCommand constructor asserts that no index is
repeated. It also did not mention the order in which a contact card
shows its tags.

This adds the order of the tags on a contact card to the UI section, the
assertion to the description of the tag command, and the storage of tags
to the Storage section. A group is not a class of its own, so the
glossary defines it as the contacts that have the same tag, and UC04
says that a group exists as soon as one contact is given the tag.
